theory.intro: Once two sides of a right-angled triangle are known, every angle in it is fixed. The inverse functions $\sin^{-1}$, $\cos^{-1}$ and $\tan^{-1}$ turn a known ratio back into the angle that produced it.
facts: The ratios are $\sin\theta=\frac{O}{H}$, $\cos\theta=\frac{A}{H}$ and $\tan\theta=\frac{O}{A}$, where $O$, $A$ and $H$ are named **relative to the marked angle**.
Choose the ratio that uses **the two sides you are given**; the third side is never needed.
If $\sin\theta=k$ then $\theta=\sin^{-1}(k)$, and likewise for $\cos^{-1}$ and $\tan^{-1}$.
On a calculator the inverse functions are the **SHIFT** (or **2nd**) functions above the trigonometric keys. Set the calculator to **degree mode** before evaluating inverse trigonometric functions.
$\sin^{-1}$ is **not** $\frac{1}{\sin}$ — it is the operation that undoes $\sin$.
Both unknown angles of a right-angled triangle are acute, so the inverse function always returns the angle you want.
$1^{\circ}=60'$, so convert a decimal answer such as $41.4096^{\circ}$ with the DMS button, rounding up when the next unit is $30$ or more.
steps: Label the sides relative to the marked angle

workedExamples.solution_text:
The rise is opposite $\theta$ and the sloping length is the hypotenuse. Use sine in degree mode.
$\begin{aligned}\sin\theta&=\frac{O}{H}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{9}{15}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{9}{15}\right)\\&\approx36.8699^{\circ}\\&\approx37^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The $8$ cm side is adjacent to $\theta$ and the $10$ cm side is the hypotenuse. Use cosine.
$\begin{aligned}\cos\theta&=\frac{A}{H}\\\cos\theta&=\frac{8}{10}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{8}{10}\right)\\&\approx36.86989765^{\circ}\\&\approx36^{\circ}52'11.63''\\&\approx36^{\circ}52'\end{aligned}$
Convert the calculator's unrounded angle to DMS. The seconds are less than $30$, so keep $52$ minutes.

The $10$ cm side is opposite $\theta$ and the $24$ cm side is adjacent. Choose tangent; the hypotenuse is not needed.
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{O}{A}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{10}{24}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{10}{24}\right)\\&\approx22.6199^{\circ}\\&\approx23^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
Sine or cosine would give the same angle using the corresponding pair of sides.

The rise is opposite $\theta$ and the horizontal run is adjacent. Use tangent.
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{2}{9}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{9}\right)\\&\approx12.5288^{\circ}\\&\approx13^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The vertical side of the right-angled triangle is the difference between the wall heights.
$\begin{aligned}h&=4.6-2.8\\&=1.8\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
The height difference is opposite $\theta$ and the horizontal span is adjacent.
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{1.8}{4.5}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1.8}{4.5}\right)\\&\approx21.80140949^{\circ}\\&\approx21^{\circ}48'5.07''\\&\approx21^{\circ}48'\end{aligned}$

mastery.question_text:
A road rises at a grade of $7$ in $24$: it rises $7$ m for every $24$ m measured horizontally.
Find the angle the road makes with the horizontal, correct to the nearest degree.
mastery.solution_text:
The rise is opposite the angle and the horizontal measurement is adjacent to it.
$\tan\theta=\frac{7}{24}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{24}\right)$
$=16.2602\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx16^{\circ}$

mastery.question_text:
A garage has a straight sloping roof joining two vertical walls of heights $5.1$ m and $2.7$ m. The horizontal distance between the walls is $4.8$ m.
Find the angle the roof makes with the horizontal, correct to the nearest minute.
mastery.solution_text:
The height difference between the walls is $5.1-2.7=2.4\text{ m}$.
The height difference is opposite the angle and the horizontal span is adjacent to it.
$\tan\theta=\frac{2.4}{4.8}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2.4}{4.8}\right)$
$=26.5650\ldots^{\circ}$
$=26^{\circ}33'54.18''$
$\approx26^{\circ}34'$
